title: Lighting
summary: The two ways to light a scene. Light objects: point (every direction, power up), spot (a cone that lights only the character), area (a square that emits) and sun (the whole scene; only its rotation matters) used as a warm back light from behind, opposite the camera. The world: its colour lights the scene too, and an environment (an HDRI: here a physical sky with the sun high over a mountain) lights it from every direction; its strength lowered a little and an area light added above. Rendered with Cycles and denoise.

objects.name: Sol
objects.description: warm sun from behind: rim light

expected_result: The scene in daylight: blue sky behind, the mushroom, pipe and bomb lit softly from above with warm rims from the sun behind them, the grass bright green.

steps.note: Shift+A > Light > Point: light in every direction; power up and move it around
type Spot: a cone above the character, only it is lit
type Area: the whole square emits
type Sun: where it is does not matter, only where it comes from: rotated to come from behind, opposite the camera: a back light; a warmer colour
World: the background colour also lights the scene (pink)
an environment texture instead of a colour: an HDRI, a 360 image that lights everything (here a physical sky: sun and atmosphere); strength lowered a little
and an area light above with a good strength
render engine: Eevee (real time; AO, bloom, screen-space reflections) or Cycles (traces every ray: realistic but noisy, so denoise on)
